english.html: ers: being another Phrynondas, of whom Aristophanes speaks, or a true Sisyphus,

notes.citation: A Latin hexameter on Sisyphus — source not identified; it adapts Homer, Iliad 6.153, where Sisyphus is "the craftiest of men" (ὃ κέρδιστος γένετ' ἀνδρῶν)
notes.original: Syſiphus in terris, quo non aſtutior alter.
notes.gloss: The line is not in the Ilias Latina in this form; it may be a humanist rendering or Coras's own.

english.html: A Sisyphus on earth, than whom none other more cunning (Sisyphus in terris, quo non astutior alter).

Inasmuch as the substitution being already discovered, he nevertheless knew so well how to impose upon the Judges, nay, even upon the said de Rols, whose husband he always said he was, that the Judges in effect released him by an interlocutory order upon contrary facts; and the woman again received him as Martin Guerre her husband.

And nevertheless, on the morrow, early in the morning, the said Pierre Guerre, joint attorney of the said de Rols, accompanied by his sons-in-law, all armed, had him made prisoner, although at that time there could be no new charges, and the said de Rols had not yet made the said Pierre Guerre her attorney to those ends: for the procuration [the power of attorney] was not made that day until the evening after vespers, as this same Pierre Guerre has himself since confessed.

He was therefore a false attorney; for so is called, in our law, not only he who has never had, either before or after, charge from the person whose attorney he says he is <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>, or indeed who once had it but has had it revoked, as he well knew <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup>; but also he who has overstepped the ends and bounds of his power, or who had no charge at the time of the execution <sup class="mk" data-key="c">c</sup>; nay, even he who had been well and legitimately appointed, if he did not know it and nevertheless did the acts of an attorney <sup class="mk" data-key="d">d</sup>. notes.original: l. ſi procura tori falſo. & i lec Accurſe, D. de cõd. ca. dau. l. licet. C. de procu.
notes.gloss: On one who has never had the mandate of the person he claims to represent; what is paid to a false procurator may be recovered.

notes.citation: Decretals, c. Ex parte decani, under a title printed de re. (perhaps De rescriptis, X 1.3, the title of note g; chapter not identified)
notes.original: c. ex parte Decani. de re.
notes.gloss: The procurator whose mandate has been revoked, and who knows it.

notes.citation: Code 6.2 (De furtis), l. Falsus (law not identified), and the Gloss and the Doctors there; the Gloss and the Masters on c. Ex parte (as note b)
notes.original: l ſulſus. & il lac les gloſe & docteurs. C. de fur. la Glo & les maiſtres au c. ex parte.
notes.gloss: The print's ſulſus is a wrong sort for falſus, the law Baldus is cited on at note g. The procurator who exceeds his mandate, or has none at the time he acts.

notes.citation: Digest 27.5.3 (De eo qui pro tutore prove curatore negotia gessit, l. Quaero; Javolenus, on one named tutor by will who acts without knowing it); Digest 46.7.3.5 (Iudicatum solvi, l. 3, § Sed et si quidem; Ulpian)
notes.original: l. quæro. D. de eo qui pro tutor. l. iij. Ꝑ.⟨alt?:P.⟩ ſed & ſi quidem. D. Iud. ſol.
notes.gloss: One who acts as guardian or procurator without knowing he has been appointed is treated as acting without mandate.

uncertain.text: l'ha euë reuoquee, comme il ſçauoit bien {b}. mais en
uncertain.note: 'euë': the final e carries two marks (a round dot left, a slanted stroke right); read as a tréma, but 'eué' is possible
the stop between 'cõd' and 'ca' is a faint low dot crossed by a paper fibre; could be read 'cõdica.' as one word
'dau.' — third letter is two minims joined below (u), no crossbar, so not 'dat.'; the abbreviation is not one I can resolve, reading given as printed
'ſulſus' is not a Latin form I can resolve and there is no stop after the opening 'l'; glyphs read ſ-u-l-ſ-u-s, a period may be lost between 'ſul' and 'ſus'
'fur.' — f has a full crossbar and the third letter has an r shoulder; 'fuſ.' cannot be ruled out at this resolution
numeral: three dots are visible but the middle minim is worn, so 'ij' is possible instead of 'iij'
final sign is a capital P with a stroke through the descender, used here as the paragraph abbreviation before the § incipit 'ſed & ſi quidem'; transcribed Ꝑ (U+A750), could be intended as §
'quæro' — the ligature is inked heavily; a plain 'a' ('quaro') is just possible
